# Theme Library v1.2 — upstream reference inventory

Verified 2026-10-12 using GitHub API against `J-X-C-Z/Design-Systems`, exact commit **f958fd2dce57b9f7650785630bb6713d8a612604**. Sources: [catalog](https://github.com/J-X-C-Z/Design-Systems/blob/f958fd2dce57b9f7650785630bb6713d8a612604/web/catalog.json), [classification](https://github.com/J-X-C-Z/Design-Systems/blob/f958fd2dce57b9f7650785630bb6713d8a612604/CLASSIFICATION.md), repository metadata, and recursive tree. The catalog itself cites an earlier reviewed commit; our inventory pins the actual fetched repository commit above.

The authoritative catalog has **22 independent language entries**: 10 at preliminary adaptation level, 12 research directions. It separately lists 172 third-party reference URLs and 24 nonlanguage candidate records; neither count is a count of installable SP themes. The upstream levels and browser claims are source statements, not SP acceptance.

Repository API `license` is **null**. This is unresolved permission, not MIT or permission inferred from public visibility. Per-package/font/image permissions require separate review. No upstream CSS, JS, images, fonts or specimen assets are shipped by this change, and the upstream repository is untouched.

The tenth entry in the current authoritative preliminary list is **midcentury-modern**. The roadmap's historical “unverified tenth” has no stable ID in its text, so that historical unnamed item's identity cannot be proven retroactively. Lumina and Noema are absent from this current catalog and remain unresolved separate names; neither is renamed or merged into MiMo, and no placeholder is counted as a shipped theme.

The remaining 12 entries are research directions (no packaged language version): Material 3 Expressive; GOV.UK 任务型公共服务语言; 命令—窗格字符界面; Classic Macintosh 桌面对象语言; 低技术·可见基础设施; Isotype 图形统计语言; 交通拓扑导视; Art Nouveau 植物线构; Art Deco 装饰几何与仪式层级; 中国手卷式游观叙事; 几何铺陈与交织装饰（伊斯兰几何传统选例）; 分格漫画叙事. Exact paths and IDs are returned by `node tools/theme-adapter.js --inventory` from `core/design-system-inventory.js`.

## Original SP examples and adapter boundary

Three **new IDs** at 1.0.0 preserve all six original built-in theme snapshots and four-page examples. The new examples are independently authored SP resources, not licensed reproductions of upstream specimens. They contain cover, content, data, image and section pages with native editable text, shape, image and chart objects. Each theme supplies full identity, visual and motion declarations. Its original-rule sourceRevision is `sp-design-language-1.0.0`, a rule release identifier, not a claim that new rules existed in an earlier Git commit. Fonts are system references only; the single embedded raster illustration is the existing original SP geometric landscape (MIT).

| SP ID | Related upstream reference | Observable SP rules | Motion |
|---|---|---|---|
| sp-editorial-language | editorial-magazine | Georgia display, wide line spacing, square bands, asymmetric cropped image | fade entrance/exit, 180/420/640ms, ease-in-out |
| sp-technical-language | precision-industrial | Courier New display, tighter body scale, two aligned columns, hard frames, contained image | directional entrance, slide transition, 120/240/360ms, linear |
| sp-warm-language | warm-illustration | Verdana display, spacious single column, rounded panels, circular chapter mark, contained image | zoom entrance intent, fade exit/transition, 260/560/800ms, ease-out |

Reference review read editorial and precision LANGUAGE.md plus warm MOTION.md at the pinned commit. These source rules describe broader semantics than the SP samples implement. The samples are modest original presentations; they do not claim upstream interaction, instrumentation, plant growth or lossless adaptation.

`adaptDesignSystemRules` accepts a validated original SP declarative manifest, a known reference ID and an explicit manual review declaration. It returns the theme and a report with pinned source, original provenance, mapping destinations, review identity and limitations. This is a reviewable mapping scaffold, not automatic extraction. It rejects missing review, unknown sources, absent designLanguage, executable fields, derived-source claims and source assets while upstream permission remains unresolved. It never reads or executes upstream CSS/JS. The CLI reads one mapping JSON and writes only stdout:

```json
{"theme":"replace this string with the complete original SP theme object","upstreamId":"editorial-magazine","review":{"decision":"original-no-source-assets","reviewer":"actual reviewing person or tool"}}
```

```sh
node tools/theme-adapter.js reviewed-mapping.json > mapping-report.json
```

Native preview entrances map declarative fade/slide/scale to existing fade-in/fade-left/zoom effects, preserving source intent in `themeMotionIntent`; exit and reduced-motion intent also remain declarative. Theme compatibility diagnostics report unsupported or approximate behaviors by renderer. Generic HTML does not faithfully play directional/zoom timelines, does not enforce all declared timing, and PPTX motion is refused. A manifest and unit test are not real editor, browser, or PowerPoint acceptance.

Validation: `node --test tests/theme-preview.test.js tests/design-system-adapter.test.js` covers all nine themes at both ratios, five-page curated content, editable native roundtrip, safe local assets, source metadata, manual mapping failure cases and unchanged six legacy theme-ref hashes.
